question: In which year did Georg Simon Ohm formulate the equation I = V/R which shows the relationship between voltage, current and resistance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1828.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A** basic law regarding flow of currents** was discovered by **Georg Simon Ohm in 1828.**
 
• Law states that the **electric current( I** )**flowing through a substance is proportional to the voltage (V) **across its ends.

 Voltage = currenttimes Resistance

 ​​V=Itimes R

 
• The **SI units of resistance is Ohm,** and is united by the **symbol Ω.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Georg Simon Ohm was a **German physicist and professor.**
 
• He was **awarded the Copley Medal of the Royal Society of London in 1841.**
 
• He became a **foreign member of the Royal Society in 1842.**
 
• He had worked for the **University of Munich.**
 
• **In 1852 **he was appointed to the **chair of physics at the University of Munich**.
